stem.text: For Groups 1 and 2, metallic bonding is stronger in metals that have a smaller atomic radius.
X and Y are both metals.
ΔHat is the energy required to produce 1.0 mol of gaseous atoms from the solid.
ΔHat X = +107 kJ mol–1; ΔHat Y = +148 kJ mol–1

explanation.text: Atomising a metal means breaking its metallic bonding, so the stronger the metallic bonding, the larger ΔHat. Y (+148) must therefore have stronger metallic bonding, i.e. a smaller atomic radius, than X (+107).

Atomic radius decreases across a period and increases down a group, so the order of radius is K > Na > Mg. That makes the strength of metallic bonding Mg > Na > K. (Mg also has two delocalised electrons per atom and a 2+ ion, which strengthens its bonding further.) The pair with Y stronger than X is X = Na, Y = Mg.

optionAnalysis.text: K has a larger radius than Na, so its metallic bonding is weaker; K would need the smaller ΔHat, not the larger one.
Correct. Mg has a smaller atomic radius than Na, so it has the stronger metallic bonding and the larger ΔHat (+148 for Y, +107 for X).
The right two metals, but the wrong way round: Mg must have the larger value, so it is Y, not X.
Mg has a much smaller radius than K, so Mg would have the larger ΔHat; this pairing puts the larger value on K.

reasoningChain: Larger ΔHat means stronger metallic bonding, which here means smaller atomic radius.
Y (+148) has the smaller radius; X (+107) has the larger.
Only option B has X = Na (larger radius, smaller value) and Y = Mg (smaller radius, larger value).

inferredMistakes.text: Getting the atomic radius trend the wrong way round across the period and choosing C.
Linking a larger atomisation energy with a larger atom.
